1. Identification Strategy
- Design: Fuzzy regression discontinuity design (FRD), centered at the 50th percentile of the 8th grade ITBS math distribution.
- Rationale:
  - Policy assignment was a deterministic rule based on a known, continuous pre-treatment score (ITBS math percentile), creating a discontinuous jump in the probability of “double-dose algebra” at the 50th percentile.
  - Compliance was strong but not perfect; thus, the discontinuity in treatment take-up is fuzzy, and the RD indicator at the cutoff serves as a valid instrument for actual receipt of the treatment bundle.
  - The FRD identifies a local average treatment effect (LATE) for marginal students near the cutoff, which is the relevant margin for policy that triages students around proficiency thresholds.
  - Longitudinal outcomes (grades, credits, PLAN/ACT, graduation, college enrollment) can be studied in reduced form (intention-to-treat) and FRD 2SLS (treatment-on-the-treated among compliers) within the same design.
  - Heterogeneity by baseline reading skills can be estimated by running subgroup FRDs or by instrumenting interactions.

2. Treatment and Control
- Treatment variable:
  - D: Indicator that the student received the CPS “double-dose algebra” package in 9th grade (two consecutive periods of algebra with the same teacher and peers, problem-solving curriculum, small-group emphasis).
  - Operationalization from transcripts/schedule: e.g., two algebra courses in grade 9 in consecutive periods or a district flag for enrollment in algebra and algebra support.
- Instrument (running variable-based assignment):
  - Z: Indicator that 8th grade ITBS math percentile < 50 (the CPS assignment rule).
- Control group (counterfactual):
  - Students just above the 50th percentile who were not assigned to double-dose and took the standard single-period algebra course.
- Treatment timing / event date:
  - Fall of 9th grade (school entry for cohorts 2003 and 2004).
- Running variable and cutoff:
  - Running variable: 8th grade ITBS math percentile (0–99).
  - Cutoff: c = 50. We will center the running variable at 50 (R = ITBSmath − 50).

3. Key Identifying Assumptions
- Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff in the absence of treatment:
  - Students just below and just above 50th percentile would have had similar outcomes absent the policy.
  - Plausibility: The score is taken in 8th grade prior to high school placement; around the cutoff there is no other policy discontinuity. We will test continuity of baseline covariates and pre-treatment characteristics.
- No precise manipulation of the running variable at the cutoff:
  - Families and schools likely cannot finely manipulate a nationally normed 8th-grade exam to sort across the 50th percentile threshold.
  - We will test for density discontinuity (McCrary test) and heaping at integer percentiles; use donut RD if necessary.
- Monotonicity (first-stage relevance without defiers):
  - Being below the cutoff weakly increases the probability of receiving double-dose for all students.
  - Plausible given district guidance and high compliance in 2003–2004; we will verify a strong positive first stage near the cutoff and by school.
- Stable treatment bundle at the cutoff:
  - The discontinuity affects the intended package (double time, peers, curriculum) and not other unrelated services exactly at c=50.
  - By design, that package is what we intend to estimate as the “treatment.” Any peer effects induced by tracking are part of the policy effect.

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
- Threat 1: Manipulation or heaping at 50
  - Mitigation: McCrary density test (rddensity); inspect rdplot of the running variable; exclude exactly 50 or ±1 percentile around the cutoff (donut RD); use bias-corrected inference robust to discrete R (rdrobust), and confirm covariate continuity.
- Threat 2: Heterogeneous compliance across schools leading to instrument endogeneity
  - Mitigation: Use FRD (Z instrumenting D) with bandwidth-local polynomial; include school and cohort indicators as covariates in covariate-adjusted rdrobust; cluster SEs at school level; check first-stage strength overall and by cohort/school; report complier shares and local first-stage.
- Threat 3: Differential attrition or mobility affecting long-run outcomes
  - Mitigation: Test for discontinuities in out-migration/dropout by 10th grade; present Lee bounds if attrition differs; show robustness using administrative NSC matches for college; report ITT alongside FRD; pre-specify primary window and report bandwidth-robustness and placebo cutoffs (e.g., 40th, 60th) to detect spurious jumps.

5. R Code Outline
Note: Replace placeholder column names with actual names in your data. Assumes a wide student-level file with 8th grade ITBS scores, demographics, transcripts-derived treatment D, outcomes, school_id, and cohort.

```r
# Packages
# install.packages(c("data.table","fixest","rdrobust","rddensity","ggplot2"))
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)
library(ggplot2)

# 1) Load data
dt <- fread("cps_longitudinal_2003_2004.csv")

# 2) Sample restrictions
# First-time 9th graders in fall 2003 or 2004; non-selective, non-alternative schools; schools with any double-dose class
dt <- dt[first_time_9th == 1 & cohort %in% c(2003, 2004) & eligible_school == 1]

# 3) Key variables
# Running variable: ITBS math percentile (0-99); center at 50
dt[, itbs_math_pct := as.numeric(itbs_math_pct)]
dt <- dt[!is.na(itbs_math_pct)]
dt[, R := itbs_math_pct - 50]
dt[, Z := as.integer(itbs_math_pct < 50)]  # assignment indicator

# Treatment indicator D: received double-dose in 9th grade (from transcript/schedule)
# If not provided, construct e.g., from having two algebra courses in grade 9
# dt[, D := as.integer(algebra_courses_9th >= 2 & consecutive_periods == 1)]
# If provided:
# dt[, D := as.integer(double_dose == 1)]
stopifnot("D" %in% names(dt))

# Outcomes
# 9th-grade algebra GPA/credits (transcript-derived)
# 10th/11th grade PLAN math; 11th grade ACT math; graduation 4/5 years; college enrollment
# Ensure outcomes are numeric/binary as appropriate
# Example names (replace with actual):
# alg_gpa9, alg_credits9, plan_math10, plan_math11, act_math11, grad4, grad5, college_enroll_any

# Baseline covariates (for covariate-adjusted RD)
covars <- c("female","race_black","race_hisp","frpl","sped",
            "itbs_read_pct","census_poverty","census_SES","cohort")

# Keep complete cases for covariate adjustment (rdrobust can take covs with NAs dropped)
for (v in covars) if (!(v %in% names(dt))) stop(paste("Missing covariate:", v))

# 4) Manipulation test: density at cutoff
dens <- rddensity(X = dt$itbs_math_pct, c = 50)
print(summary(dens))

# 5) Covariate balance checks at cutoff (reduced-form RDs)
for (v in covars) {
  cat("\nCovariate continuity test for", v, "\n")
  print(summary(rdrobust(y = dt[[v]], x = dt$itbs_math_pct, c = 50,
                         covs = NULL, kernel = "triangular",
                         bwselect = "mserd", vce = "hc")))
}

# 6) First-stage (treatment take-up at cutoff)
fs <- rdrobust(y = dt$D, x = dt$itbs_math_pct, c = 50,
               covs = dt[, ..covars], kernel = "triangular",
               bwselect = "mserd", vce = "hc",
               cluster = dt$school_id)
print(summary(fs))
# Plot treatment take-up
rdplot(y = dt$D, x = dt$itbs_math_pct, c = 50, title = "First-stage: Double-dose vs ITBS math percentile")

# 7) Main FRD estimates for outcomes
outcomes <- c("alg_gpa9","alg_credits9","plan_math10","plan_math11","act_math11",
              "grad4","grad5","college_enroll_any")

frd_results <- lapply(outcomes, function(yvar) {
  cat("\nFRD for outcome:", yvar, "\n")
  out <- rdrobust(y = dt[[yvar]], x = dt$itbs_math_pct, c = 50,
                  fuzzy = dt$D, covs = dt[, ..covars],
                  kernel = "triangular", bwselect = "mserd", vce = "hc",
                  cluster = dt$school_id)
  print(summary(out))
  return(out)
})

# 8) ITT (reduced form) for completeness
itt_results <- lapply(outcomes, function(yvar) {
  cat("\nReduced-form ITT for outcome:", yvar, "\n")
  out <- rdrobust(y = dt[[yvar]], x = dt$itbs_math_pct, c = 50,
                  covs = dt[, ..covars], kernel = "triangular",
                  bwselect = "mserd", vce = "hc",
                  cluster = dt$school_id)
  print(summary(out))
  return(out)
})

# 9) Heterogeneity by baseline reading skill (e.g., below vs above median ITBS reading percentile)
read_med <- median(dt$itbs_read_pct, na.rm = TRUE)
dt[, read_low := as.integer(itbs_read_pct < read_med)]

for (grp in c(0,1)) {
  dts <- dt[read_low == grp]
  cat("\nHeterogeneity FRD - read_low =", grp, "\n")
  for (yvar in outcomes) {
    out <- rdrobust(y = dts[[yvar]], x = dts$itbs_math_pct, c = 50,
                    fuzzy = dts$D, covs = dts[, ..covars],
                    kernel = "triangular", bwselect = "mserd", vce = "hc",
                    cluster = dts$school_id)
    print(summary(out))
  }
}

# 10) Robustness: Donut RD (drop |R| < 1 percentile point)
dt_donut <- dt[abs(R) >= 1]
for (yvar in outcomes) {
  cat("\nDonut FRD for outcome:", yvar, "\n")
  out <- rdrobust(y = dt_donut[[yvar]], x = dt_donut$itbs_math_pct, c = 50,
                  fuzzy = dt_donut$D, covs = dt_donut[, ..covars],
                  kernel = "triangular", bwselect = "mserd", vce = "hc",
                  cluster = dt_donut$school_id)
  print(summary(out))
}

# 11) Placebo cutoffs (no policy at 40th and 60th percentiles)
placebo_cuts <- c(40, 60)
for (c0 in placebo_cuts) {
  cat("\nPlacebo FRD at cutoff", c0, "\n")
  for (yvar in outcomes) {
    out <- rdrobust(y = dt[[yvar]], x = dt$itbs_math_pct, c = c0,
                    fuzzy = dt$D, covs = dt[, ..covars],
                    kernel = "triangular", bwselect = "mserd", vce = "hc",
                    cluster = dt$school_id)
    print(summary(out))
  }
}

# 12) Optional: Attainment vs test-score “predictive check”
# Compare observed FRD effect on grad5 to FRD effect on act_math11
frd_act <- rdrobust(y = dt$act_math11, x = dt$itbs_math_pct, c = 50,
                    fuzzy = dt$D, covs = dt[, ..covars],
                    kernel = "triangular", bwselect = "mserd", vce = "hc",
                    cluster = dt$school_id)
frd_grad <- rdrobust(y = dt$grad5, x = dt$itbs_math_pct, c = 50,
                     fuzzy = dt$D, covs = dt[, ..covars],
                     kernel = "triangular", bwselect = "mserd", vce = "hc",
                     cluster = dt$school_id)
beta_act <- summary(frd_act)$coef[1,1]  # LATE on ACT
beta_grad <- summary(frd_grad)$coef[1,1] # LATE on graduation
cat("\nRatio of LATEs (grad per ACT SD):", beta_grad / beta_act, "\n")
```

6. Expected Results
- Short-run course performance: Positive and sizable improvements for marginal students near the cutoff (e.g., +0.15 to +0.30 GPA points in 9th grade algebra; higher probability of earning algebra credits on time).
- Standardized test scores (PLAN/ACT): Modest gains (e.g., 0.05–0.15 SD) given the problem-solving focus and potential misalignment with tested content.
- High school graduation: Meaningful increases via improved on-track status and credit accumulation (e.g., +4 to +8 percentage points within five years).
- College enrollment: Smaller but positive effects (e.g., +2 to +5 percentage points) through improved graduation and readiness.
- Heterogeneity: Larger gains for students with weaker baseline reading skills if the support class emphasizes verbal exposition and structured problem solving; at minimum, no worse outcomes for higher readers.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)
- C1: No precise manipulation of the running variable at the cutoff — 1
  - We will run a McCrary density test and donut RD; institutional features limit manipulation.
- C2: Continuity of baseline covariates at the cutoff — 1
  - We will test each pre-determined covariate using RD; expect smoothness.
- C3: Correct functional form and bandwidth choice — 1
  - Use rdrobust with bias-corrected inference, data-driven bandwidth, triangular kernel, and local linear; show robustness to alternative bandwidths and donut.
- C4: Strong first stage for the FRD — 1
  - Compliance was high in 2003–2004; we will document a clear discontinuity in take-up and report F-statistics/first-stage jumps.
- C5: Stable treatment construct and no other discontinuities at c=50 — 1
  - The policy bundle is well-defined and triggered only by ITBS math <50; placebo cutoffs will check for other jumps.

Notes on interpretation:
- Estimates are LATEs for compliers near the 50th percentile in cohorts 2003–2004 at eligible CPS schools. They capture the total effect of the treatment bundle (time, pedagogy, and peer composition), including any within-school equilibrium adjustments.
